claims.claim: in a random sample of 203 northeastern lakes (EMAP, 1991–96): brown bullhead 69 %, white sucker 56 %, banded killifish 26 %, American eel 19 % of lakes (Whittier et al. 2001, abstract)
claims.note: full text not obtained. The abstract: 'Brown bullhead and white sucker ... collected in 69% and 56% of the sampled lakes'; 'Banded killifish, American eel, and yellow bullhead ... 26%, 19% and 17%'; 203 randomly selected lakes in eight states. The paper already says 'abstracts only'

notes: Needs the article (JSTOR 10.2307/3858449 or BioOne). The abstract also summarises all 88 species of the EMAP Northeast Lakes survey and gives yellow bullhead 17 %. The §3.5.1 follow-on mention ('Whittier et al. 1997') belongs to Whittier_etal_1997. Halliwell's 2019 draft (secondary) ranks brown bullhead 4th, white sucker 5th, banded killifish 10th and American eel 14th most widespread, citing this paper — consistent with the abstract's order.
